title: abstract_text truncation uses chars().take(end) but end is a byte offset
description: posting.rs:1170-1178, delivery.rs:348-352. The auto-generated abstract_text for long posts computes 'end' using text.find(". ") which returns a byte offset. Then it does text.chars().take(end).collect(). The .take(end) treats 'end' as a character count, not a byte offset. For ASCII text this is identical, but for multi-byte UTF-8 text (e.g., CJK, emoji), chars().take(byte_offset) will take fewer characters than intended because byte_offset > char_count for multi-byte text. The abstract will be shorter than expected but not incorrectly truncated. Same pattern exists in delivery.rs:348-352.
